meta.note: 1 aureus = 25 denarii = 100 sestertii (HS) = 400 asses. Denarius under Trajan is c. 3.4 g at c. 85-90% fine, so c. 3.0 g fine silver. Prices marked [C] are the author's derived estimates and are the weakest numbers in this project. Bulk metal prices are anchored to silver using ratios implied by the Edict of Diocletian (301 AD), used for RATIOS ONLY because the Edict's own unit is a collapsed currency 200 years later.

confidence_key.B: probable, scholarly consensus, contested in detail

wage_rates_denarii_per_hour._note: Assumes a 10-hour working day and c. 250 working days per year, so 2500 worker-hours per person-year. Roman festival days are numerous; 250 is already generous.

chemist.note: does not exist yet; you must create this trade

machinist.note: does not exist yet; you must create this trade

mason.note: Rome has these in abundance and they are good.

millwright.note: Water-mill builder. Rome has them; they are the scarcest useful trade you can hire.

plumber.note: Lead worker. Roman plumbarii are skilled and numerous.

merchant.note: Agent and factor, paid on commission in practice.

engraver.note: Die and seal cutter. Rome has excellent ones; they become your punchcutters.

optician.note: DOES NOT EXIST YET. You must create this trade from glassworkers.

engineer.note: DOES NOT EXIST as a paid civilian profession. Rome has military and hydraulic engineers under state employ; a private one is your invention.

electrician.note: DOES NOT EXIST. Cannot exist until Module 50 does.

silver_kg.note: Definitional: 1 den = c. 3.15 g fine silver at 100 AD.

gold_kg.note: From the aureus at c. 7.27 g = 25 den. Implied gold:silver c. 11:1.

mercury_kg.note: Anchored to Pliny NH 33.118, which reports the price of minium (cinnabar pigment) fixed by law at 70 sesterces per Roman pound of 324 g, i.e. c. 54 den/kg. Metallic mercury should be comparable or dearer. Almaden is an imperial monopoly, so access is a political problem before it is a price problem.

calamine_kg.note: ore at the mine, not contained metal; previously overpriced at 0.50

fluorspar_kg.note: not a traded commodity; you will have to source it yourself

silk_kg.note: Silk Road; Pliny complains of the bullion drain east

shellac_kg.note: Indian Ocean trade via Berenice-Muziris; 1-3 year lead time

copper_ore_kg.note: ore at the mine at c. 3-8% Cu

cinnabar_kg.note: Pliny NH 33.118: minium price-fixed at 70 HS per Roman pound.

bauxite_kg.note: not a Roman commodity; you will identify and open the deposit yourself

manure_kg.note: effectively free, but cartage is not

salt_kg.note: cheap and taxed; Ostia salt pans

cryolite_kg.note: Greenland is unreachable; assume a synthetic fluoride bath from your own HF

flue_dust_kg.note: a waste stream from your own zinc smelter; cost is handling only

graphite_kg.note: high purity; you will make it, not buy it

zinc_kg.note: does not exist until you make it; price is your own cost

nickel_kg.note: not isolated in antiquity; a late-programme item

tungsten_kg.note: needs the arc furnace; do not plan around it early

platinum_g.note: South American platinum is unreachable; Ural and alluvial sources only, effectively unobtainable in quantity

germanium_g.note: INTERNAL TRANSFER PRICE ONLY, to keep downstream nodes from looking free. The real cost of germanium is the extraction and purification plant, which is already costed in germanium_extraction, gecl4_purification and ge_reduction. Do not add these together and call it the cost of germanium.

sulfuric_acid_kg.note: internal transfer price; retort route is ~5x this, chamber route ~0.4x

nitre_kg.note: your own nitre beds; there is no market for this in Rome

argon_or_h2_m3.note: argon is not separable for you; use purified hydrogen or nitrogen

cast_iron_kg.note: Cheaper per kilogramme than wrought bar because it comes straight from the furnace without the finery. Brittle: useless in tension.

aluminium_kg.note: Post-electrolysis price. BEFORE the electrical age aluminium is a precious metal worth roughly 2,000 den/kg, dearer than silver, and Napoleon III served guests on it. The price collapse when Hall-Heroult arrives is one of the largest in the history of materials.

paper_kg.note: Your own production cost once the mill runs. Compare papyrus at roughly 10x per unit area and parchment at far more.

essential_oil_kg.note: Blended average. Attar of roses is worth many times this and is one of the highest-margin products available to you in year two.

water_kg.note: Free at the aqueduct, which is a genuine Roman advantage. Priced at zero so that recipes can state their water honestly without distorting cost.

rubber_kg.note: UNOBTAINABLE, priced at an absurd number deliberately so that any recipe depending on it shows up instantly as impossible. Natural rubber is American. There is no route. Use mat_synthetic_rubber, which sits behind a full petrochemical industry, or accept leather, shellac, oiled linen and bitumen and be honest about how much worse they are.

wool_kg.note: Greasy fleece to scoured. Rome's largest textile input by far.

rose_petals_kg.note: About 3,000 kg of petals yields roughly 1 kg of attar, which is why attar is worth more than silver by weight and is one of the best products you can make in year two.

phosphorus_red_kg.note: Red allotrope. The white form is what caused phosphorus necrosis of the jaw in match workers, a genuine industrial atrocity you know how to avoid.

rubber_tubing_kg.note: UNOBTAINABLE, see rubber_kg. Substitute: lead pipe, glass tube with ground joints, or oiled leather.

monochromatic_light_kg.note: Not a material. A sodium flame costs nothing; priced at zero so recipes can name it honestly.

transport_multipliers._note: Multiply delivered cost. The single most important economic fact in the Empire: put every facility on navigable water.

road_per_100km.note: grain roughly doubles in price over c. 500 km of road haulage

starting_kit_options._note: What you carry back. Chosen to be sellable without being visibly anachronistic. Value in denarii at 100 AD prices.

items: unmarked gold in rough ingot and dust form
a bound codex of notes in Greek (this guide)
a small steel knife and files (explain as Noric or Indian work)
seeds: none from the Americas; do not attempt
a small quantity of high-purity chemical reagents as 'Egyptian samples'

merchant_rich.note: Enough to buy an estate and a workshop immediately, but a stranger arriving with an equestrian fortune in unminted gold attracts the fiscus. Higher start, higher suspicion.
